examInfo.format: NASM describes the NASM-CPT exam as 120 multiple choice questions with four answer choices, taken in 2 hours. Only 100 questions are scored; the other 20 are unscored pretest questions that are mixed in. This practice mock covers the 100 scored questions across the six exam domains.

passCriteria.description: You need a scaled score of 70 (on a 0 to 100 scale) to pass. Scaled scores convert your raw score so different exam forms can be compared, so 70 is not exactly 70 correct answers. There is no separate minimum score for each domain.

content.eligibility: Check NASM's current requirements before you register, including the minimum age, education, and CPR/AED requirements. The exam is closed-book and proctored, and it can be taken online or in person.
content.intro: The NASM Certified Personal Trainer (NASM-CPT) exam tests the knowledge a new personal trainer needs to work safely with clients. It covers six domains: Exercise Technique and Training Instruction (24%), Program Design (20%), Assessment (16%), Basic and Applied Sciences and Nutritional Concepts (15%), Client Relations and Behavioral Coaching (15%), and Professional Development and Responsibility (10%). Short practice sets help you remember the OPT model phases, assessment findings, and scope of practice rules.
content.trendSummary: The two biggest domains, Exercise Technique and Program Design, make up 44% of the scored questions. Topics that are easy to mix up include the five OPT phases and their reps and rest, overhead squat assessment findings (which muscles are overactive or underactive), planes of motion, and what a trainer may and may not do within their scope of practice. The chapters on this site are study groupings of those domains.
content.studyTip: Start with the OPT model and the overhead squat assessment, because many other topics connect to them. Then practice exercise technique, planes of motion, and scope of practice in short Beginner sets. When you can answer most Intermediate questions, take a full 100-question Mock Exam and review every miss.

faqs.question: How many questions are on the NASM-CPT exam?
faqs.answer: The exam has 120 multiple choice questions. 100 are scored and 20 are unscored pretest questions. You get 2 hours.

faqs.question: What score do I need to pass the NASM-CPT exam?
faqs.answer: You need a scaled score of 70. A scaled score converts your raw score so that different exam forms can be compared.

faqs.question: What topics does the exam cover?
faqs.answer: Six domains: Exercise Technique and Training Instruction (24%), Program Design (20%), Assessment (16%), Basic and Applied Sciences and Nutritional Concepts (15%), Client Relations and Behavioral Coaching (15%), and Professional Development and Responsibility (10%).

faqs.question: Are these the real NASM exam questions?
faqs.answer: No. Every question here is an original practice question. The real exam questions are confidential, so use this site for practice and study NASM's own materials too.

faqs.question: Is this site connected to NASM?
faqs.answer: No. This site is independent and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by NASM.

studyTips.studyOrder: Start with The OPT Model and Its Phases in Program Design, then Movement and Posture Assessment, because many questions build on them. Next study the three Exercise Technique chapters, which together are the largest domain at 24 of 100 scored questions. Finish with Anatomy and Biomechanics, Motivation and Behavior Change, and Scope of Practice and Ethics.
studyTips.hardChapters: The OPT Model and Its Phases is full of details that sound alike, such as which phase pairs strength with stabilization and which pairs strength with power, plus rep ranges and rest times. Movement and Posture Assessment asks which muscles are overactive or underactive for each squat compensation, so make a table and review it often. Anatomy and Biomechanics also trips people up on planes of motion and muscle roles.
studyTips.examDay: The exam has 120 questions in 2 hours, and 20 of them are unscored, so you cannot tell which ones count. Treat every question the same and aim for about one minute each. You need a scaled score of 70 to pass. When a question asks what a trainer should do, choose the answer that keeps the client safe and stays within a trainer's scope of practice.
